intro: Buying a home in Montana requires careful consideration of mortgage payments, property taxes, insurance premiums and ongoing maintenance expenses. Recent changes to Montana's property tax system also make it important to understand how residential properties are classified.

Our free Montana mortgage calculator helps you estimate your monthly housing payment using your home price, down payment, interest rate and loan term. Whether you're purchasing in Billings, Missoula, Bozeman, Great Falls or a smaller Montana community, compare financing scenarios before committing to a property.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Montana?

blocks.markdown:
A $375,000 Montana home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed annual interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $1,798.65.

An illustrative monthly housing payment breakdown is shown below.
This example assumes no private mortgage insurance or HOA fees. Taxes, insurance premiums and the interest rate are illustrative planning assumptions rather than verified statewide averages.

Montana offers housing opportunities across metropolitan communities, mountain towns, agricultural regions and rural areas.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Montana QuickFacts](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/MT/LFE041223), the median value of owner-occupied homes was $375,800 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among homeowners with mortgages were $1,798, while approximately 69.2% of occupied housing units were owner-occupied.

These historical figures provide useful context for homebuyers but do not represent current property asking prices.

Properties in Bozeman and popular mountain communities may have different purchase prices from comparable homes in eastern Montana.

Research recent property sales within your preferred neighborhood. Consider employment access, utilities, transportation and insurance availability when establishing your purchase budget.

sections.heading: How to Use the Montana Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Start by entering the expected purchase price of your property and the amount you plan to contribute as a down payment.

Select your repayment period and enter the annual interest rate quoted by your lender.

Next, provide the property's estimated annual tax liability and homeowners insurance premiums. Include monthly association dues and applicable private mortgage insurance.

Review the estimated monthly housing payment and adjust your inputs to compare financing arrangements.

For example, increasing your down payment reduces your borrowing amount and may eliminate conventional mortgage insurance requirements.

The amortization schedule helps you understand how your mortgage balance decreases over time and how much interest you could pay throughout the repayment period.

Use our national Mortgage Calculator to compare financing scenarios in other states.

sections.heading: How Montana Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
Montana's property tax system underwent significant changes affecting residential properties in the 2026 tax year.

The revised system provides different property tax classifications and rates depending on how a property is used.

Qualifying primary residences and long-term rental properties may benefit from reduced, graduated rates.

### Montana residential property tax rates for 2026

According to the [Montana Department of Revenue's 2026 property tax guidance](https://revenue.mt.gov/property/property-tax-changes/2026-property-tax-information), qualifying homesteads and applicable long-term rental properties use the following tiered rates:

The rates apply incrementally. A higher property value does not automatically cause the entire property's value to be calculated using the highest applicable rate.

These percentages determine taxable value before applicable mill levies are applied. They are not the property's final effective annual tax rate.

### Montana property tax calculation example

Consider a qualifying homestead with an assessed market value of $500,000.

The first $378,000 falls within the 0.76% bracket. The remaining $122,000 falls within the 0.90% bracket.

Assuming a hypothetical combined levy of 500 mills, annual property taxes would be:

$3,970.80 × 500 ÷ 1,000 = $1,985.40

This represents approximately $165.45 per month.

The example excludes special assessments, additional charges and other applicable adjustments. Obtain a property-specific estimate before entering annual taxes into the calculator.

### Primary residences versus second homes

Under the revised system, ordinary residential properties that do not qualify for homestead or long-term rental treatment generally use a flat classification rate of 1.90%.

This can include second homes, short-term rentals and vacant residential lots.

Consequently, two similarly valued properties may have considerably different tax obligations depending on their classification.

Review the [Montana homestead and long-term rental guidance](https://revenue.mt.gov/property/property-tax-changes/homesteads-and-long-term-rentals) to understand occupancy, enrollment and eligibility requirements.

Do not assume that the previous owner's preferential classification automatically applies to you.

### Montana property tax assistance

The [Property Tax Assistance Program](https://www.revenue.mt.gov/property/property-tax-help/ptap) provides qualifying homeowners with reductions based on income, marital status, ownership and occupancy requirements.

Eligible applicants may receive reductions of 30%, 50% or 80% in the applicable property tax rate under program rules.

Income thresholds and other conditions can change annually. Confirm your eligibility before incorporating potential tax savings into your mortgage estimate.

Insurance premiums depend on property location, construction materials, rebuilding costs and environmental exposure.

Montana homeowners may experience wildfires, hailstorms, heavy snowfall, freezing temperatures and flooding.

Obtain insurance quotes before completing your property purchase.

### Wildfire insurance considerations

Homes near forests, grasslands and mountainous areas may face additional wildfire exposure.

Ask insurers whether the property's location affects coverage availability, premiums or required mitigation measures.

Review the property's roof materials, surrounding vegetation and accessibility for emergency services.

A property with a relatively affordable purchase price may become less attractive if suitable insurance is difficult or expensive to obtain.

### Flood and winter weather coverage

Ordinary homeowners insurance generally excludes flooding.

Properties near rivers, streams and low-lying areas may require separate flood coverage.

Use the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home) to investigate potential exposure.

Montana homeowners should also review coverage conditions relating to frozen pipes, roof damage and winter weather.

Include all applicable annual insurance premiums in your mortgage estimate without counting overlapping coverage twice.
The following estimates assume a 20% down payment, a 6% fixed annual interest rate and a 30-year mortgage.

These figures exclude property taxes, insurance, mortgage insurance and association fees.

Use the complete Montana mortgage calculator to compare monthly expenses associated with individual properties.

The Montana Board of Housing offers mortgage financing and down payment assistance through approved participating lenders.

### Regular Bond Loan Program

The [Montana Regular Bond Loan Program](https://commerce.mt.gov/Housing/Lenders-and-Real-Estate-Agents/Regular-Bond-Loan-Program) provides eligible buyers with 30-year mortgage financing.

Applicants generally must meet household income, purchase price, occupancy and first-time homebuyer requirements.

The program is available for qualifying properties throughout Montana, including certain manufactured homes and condominiums.

### Bond Advantage down payment assistance

The [Bond Advantage assistance program](https://www.commerce.mt.gov/Housing/Homeownership/Down-Payment-Assistance) provides qualifying borrowers with assistance of up to 5% of the purchase price, capped at $15,000.

The assistance takes the form of a 15-year second mortgage carrying the same fixed interest rate as the associated first mortgage.

Applicants generally need a minimum credit score of 620, approved homebuyer education and a minimum $1,000 contribution toward the purchase.

Include the second mortgage payment when estimating your complete housing expenses.

### MBOH Plus deferred assistance

The MBOH Plus program also provides assistance of up to 5% of the purchase price, capped at $15,000.

Unlike Bond Advantage, this option carries no interest or scheduled monthly payments.

Its published household income limits are $80,000 for households of one or two people and $90,000 for households of three or more.

Additional lending, education and borrower contribution requirements apply.

Repayment becomes due when qualifying events occur, including property sale, refinancing or repayment of the primary mortgage.

Review the [Montana Board of Housing's current financing rates and eligibility limits](https://commerce.mt.gov/Housing/Homeownership/Current-Rates-Income-and-Purchase-Price-Limits) before selecting a mortgage.

sections.heading: Additional Costs of Owning a Montana Home

blocks.markdown:
Montana homeowners should prepare for expenses beyond their regular mortgage payments.

Winter heating, snow removal, roof maintenance and transportation can affect household budgets.

Rural and mountain properties may require private well maintenance, septic system servicing, access road repairs or additional wildfire mitigation.

Request historical utility bills and investigate maintenance obligations before purchasing.

Buyers considering properties far from employment centers should account for commuting distances and vehicle expenses.

Maintain emergency savings rather than committing all available funds to the down payment.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Montana?

blocks.markdown:
Begin with reliable monthly take-home income and subtract existing debt payments, household expenses and savings contributions.

Our [Montana Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/montana-paycheck-calculator/) can help estimate after-tax earnings, while our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) can help evaluate existing financial obligations.

Allow sufficient room for insurance deductibles, repairs and seasonal heating expenses.

Compare mortgage offers using the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/).

Choose a property whose complete housing expenses remain manageable alongside your other financial priorities.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $375,000 Montana home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, principal and interest would be approximately $1,798.65 monthly. Property taxes, insurance and applicable fees increase the total housing payment.

### How did Montana property taxes change in 2026?

Montana introduced reduced, graduated classification rates for qualifying homesteads and certain long-term rental properties. Other ordinary residential properties generally use a flat 1.90% classification rate. Local mill levies still determine the resulting property tax liability.

### Does Montana offer down payment assistance?

Yes. The Montana Board of Housing offers qualifying borrowers up to $15,000 through Bond Advantage and MBOH Plus assistance programs. These are secondary loans with different repayment arrangements and eligibility requirements.

Use our Montana mortgage calculator to compare home prices, interest rates, down payments and repayment periods.

Replace illustrative property taxes and insurance premiums with verified property-specific estimates. Understanding Montana's updated tax classifications and complete homeownership expenses can help you establish a sustainable purchase budget.
